say.text: Psoas is a hip flexor, and a retrocaecal appendix lies on top of it. Ask which hip movement loads the muscle.
Yes. Extending the right hip stretches the psoas. Pain on that movement suggests a retrocaecal appendix lying on the muscle.
Retrocaecal is the commonest position of the appendix, so this is the sign you will meet most often.

A young woman has sudden mid-cycle RIF pain. There is no migration, she is afebrile and her count is normal. The pain settles over a few hours.
Most likely diagnosis?
Mid-cycle pain with a normal count and no migration does not follow the appendix pattern. Which condition in women causes mid-cycle pain?
Yes. Mittelschmerz is pain from a ruptured Graafian follicle at mid-cycle, a women's look-alike of appendicitis.

Look-alikes differ by group. Children: mesenteric lymphadenitis, Meckel's diverticulitis. Women: ectopic pregnancy, ovarian cyst, pelvic inflammatory disease. Adults: ureteric colic, caecal diverticulitis, Crohn's.
Appendicitis is one item on each list, so ask who the patient is before you settle on it.
